description:
Analyze the SMTP capture file at /home/ga/Documents/captures/smtp.pcap and produce a structured forensics report.

Extract the following information and write it to a plain-text report file at /home/ga/Documents/smtp_report.txt. Each field must appear on its own line in exactly the format 'field_name: value' (one space after the colon).

Required fields:
1. total_packets — Total number of packets in the entire capture file.
2. smtp_packets — Number of packets identified as SMTP protocol.
3. sender — The email address from the SMTP MAIL FROM command. Write only the email address (e.g. user@example.com), without angle brackets or the FROM: prefix.
4. recipient — The email address from the SMTP RCPT TO command. Write only the email address, without angle brackets or the TO: prefix.
5. smtp_server_ip — IPv4 address of the SMTP server (the host that sends the 220 service-ready greeting).
6. smtp_client_ip — IPv4 address of the SMTP client (the host that initiates the connection).

Example output format:
total_packets: 42
smtp_packets: 20
sender: alice@example.com
recipient: bob@example.com
smtp_server_ip: 192.168.1.1
smtp_client_ip: 192.168.1.2

Wireshark is already open with smtp.pcap loaded. You may use the GUI, tshark, or any tools available.
